title: IndiGo Swings to Rs 382 Crore Q1 Loss as Fuel Costs Surge 86%
excerpt: India's largest airline reported a sharp reversal from Rs 2,161 crore profit a year ago, with crude oil above $100 per barrel driven by the Iran conflict pushing expenses 35% higher even as revenue grew 20%.
body:
InterGlobe Aviation, the operator of IndiGo, reported a first-quarter net loss of Rs 382 crore ($39.6 million) for the three months ended June 30, a stark reversal from the Rs 2,161 crore profit it recorded in the same period last year, according to Reuters.

The loss marks IndiGo's second consecutive quarterly deficit after a Rs 2,662 crore loss in Q4 FY26. Despite posting 20% revenue growth to Rs 24,584 crore, expenses ran ahead at 35.1%, driven almost entirely by a punishing fuel bill.

Fuel Bill Nearly Doubles

Aircraft fuel expenses surged 86% to Rs 10,830 crore as the Iran conflict sent Brent crude above $100 per barrel during the quarter. IndiGo does not hedge its fuel costs, a policy that left margins fully exposed to the price spike.

"We will be putting our minds to start looking at whether fuel hedging is another option...given what we've experienced in the last three months now."

— Gaurav Negi, Chief Financial Officer, IndiGo

The airline said last quarter it would explore hedging through financial contracts that lock in fuel prices, but has yet to implement any mechanism. IndiGo's lack of protection has translated directly into margin erosion across two consecutive quarters.

Rupee Weakness Compounds the Pain

More than 60% of IndiGo's costs — including aircraft leases, maintenance, and parts — are directly or indirectly denominated in US dollars. With the rupee trading near 96.55 to the dollar, steady depreciation over the past year has inflated operating expenses further.

In Q4 FY26, this currency mismatch produced a Rs 4,882 crore foreign-exchange loss alone, compared with a Rs 138 crore gain a year earlier. The same structural exposure continued into Q1 FY27, compounding fuel-driven cost pressures.

Revenue Growth Cannot Keep Pace

Quarterly revenue of Rs 24,584 crore represented strong 20% year-on-year growth, supported by higher ticket prices and IndiGo's continued domestic dominance. The airline now commands a record 66.3% share of India's domestic aviation market, according to recent traffic data.

But analysts had expected the airline to remain profitable. Pre-results estimates from JM Financial projected profit after tax of Rs 657 crore, while other brokerages forecast around Rs 1,084 crore. The actual loss was a significant miss, underscoring how rapidly fuel costs overwhelmed the demand picture.

Walsh Era Begins August 3

The results carry added significance as the final quarterly earnings before incoming CEO Willie Walsh takes charge on August 3. Walsh, the former head of British Airways parent International Airlines Group and outgoing IATA director general, replaces Pieter Elbers, who resigned earlier this year following an operational crisis.

Investors will watch Walsh's strategy closely. He inherits an airline that dominates domestically but faces significant headwinds on international routes, where the Pakistan airspace ban and Middle East conflict have increased flight times and costs.

"While the near term remains volatile, we remain firmly focused on disciplined execution, cost efficiency, and long-term value creation."

— Rahul Bhatia, Managing Director, IndiGo

IndiGo is phasing out older, less fuel-efficient damp-leased aircraft and has guided capacity growth of just 3-4% for Q1 FY27, down sharply from 16.4% in the year-ago period. The airline operates more than 440 aircraft to over 40 international destinations.

What to Watch

The immediate question is whether IndiGo will implement actual fuel hedging contracts before next quarter. With crude prices elevated and the rupee under pressure from foreign outflows tied to the oil shock, the same cost dynamics are likely to persist. Walsh's strategy reset will need to balance cost management with the carrier's long-term international expansion ambitions.
